claim_boundary: This experiment generates severity-conditioned future-like scalp scenarios rather than asserting true longitudinal prediction.

datasets.title: UniDataPro men hair-loss dataset
datasets.limitation: Public dataset card needs audit for demographic balance and label provenance.

datasets.title: UniDataPro women hair-loss dataset
datasets.limitation: Requires label harmonisation with Norwood-style staging before pooled training.

datasets.title: Hair loss male Norwood scale
datasets.limitation: Likely biased toward web-scraped top-view examples with uneven acquisition conditions.

datasets.title: Dataset of bald people
datasets.limitation: Proxy labels and broad web variability may reduce label cleanliness.

conditioning.rationale: The baseline keeps conditioning narrow so that target-stage sensitivity can be evaluated before broader multimodal covariates are introduced.

compute_environment.scaling_note: Resolution 256x256, batch size 4, and the single-GPU setup are feasibility-checked defaults for the first run. They may be scaled if later compute access and project time permit.

hypotheses.primary: A latent diffusion model conditioned on current severity and target severity will generate scalp images whose derived severity predictions increase monotonically as the target severity increases.
secondary:
Conditioning on target severity will outperform an unconditioned baseline on severity-consistency checks and LPIPS.
Temperature scaling on the auxiliary severity head will reduce ECE on the held-out test split without materially worsening Brier score.
